extracted.intended_audience: inventors, patent applicants, patent agents/attorneys, patent examiners, and government officials dealing with patents in Indonesia
extracted.subtask_description: Legal standards and procedural requirements for obtaining, maintaining, exploiting, and enforcing patents (and simple patents) in Indonesia: substantive patentability criteria, excluded subject matter, application formalities, examination, grant/refusal, rights/obligations of patent holders, prior user and government-use rules, timelines, fees, and enforcement provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent means an exclusive right granted to the inventors by the State as the result of his/her invention in the field of technology for a definite period of time to exclusively implement his/her given invention or to give consent to other party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes that patents are state-granted exclusive rights in the technological field, transferable or licensable; duration rules appear elsewhere (Article 22).

rubrics_metrics.name: Invention (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Invention means an idea of an inventor embodied into a specific problem solving activity in the field of technology in the form of product or process, or refining and developing product or process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines eligible subject-matter baseline: product or process, including improvements and refinements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentable subject-matter (Article 3 for Patent)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Patent is granted for a new invention, involving inventive steps, and susceptible to industrial application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Three-part substantive test: novelty, inventive step (non-obviousness), and industrial applicability (utility/industrial implementation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Simple patent subject-matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Simple Patent is granted for a new invention, an improvement from existing product or process, and susceptible to industrial application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simple Patent has a lower threshold (allows improvements) and different term (Article 23).

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty (Article 5)
rubrics_metrics.description: An Invention is deemed to be novel ... given that on the Filing Date, pertinent Invention is not similar to any previously disclosed technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Previously disclosed technology includes publication anywhere, verbal disclosure, demonstration, use, or other ways enabling a skilled person to implement the invention before the filing or priority date; includes previously published application documents with earlier filing dates in Indonesia.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions to novelty loss (grace periods)
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 6 months prior to the Filing Date, the Invention is not deemed to have been published if it was displayed at an official or recognized exhibition, used by the inventor for experimentation, or published by the inventor at academic assemblies; also not deemed published if published by others within 12 months through breach of confidentiality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limited grace for inventor disclosures via exhibitions, experimental use, academic defense; includes remedy for confidentiality breaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive step / non-obviousness (Article 7)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Invention involves inventive steps if ... to a person skilled in the technical field constitutes to be non-obvious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obviousness evaluation must take into account the state of the art at the time of filing or first priority filing; standard is the skilled person test.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial applicability (Article 8)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Invention may be industrially applicable if the Invention can be implemented in the industry as described in the Application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires enabling disclosure showing industrial implementation; aligns with sufficiency/enabling requirement in Article 25(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Excluded subject matter (general) (Article 4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventions do not include: esthetical creation; scheme; rules and methods in conducting activity involving mental activity, games, and business; rules and methods containing only computer program; presentation of information; discoveries in the form of new use of existing known product or new forms from existing compound without significantly enhanced efficacy and different known chemical structures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerates non-patentable categories (abstract, business/methods, pure software as such, information presentations, certain discoveries).

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-patentable inventions (Article 9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventions which cannot be granted Patent include: processes/products whose publication/usage contravenes law, morality or public order; methods of examination, treatment, medication, and/or surgery applied to humans and/or animals; theories and methods in the field of science and mathematics; all living organisms except microorganisms; biological processes essential to produce plants or animals except non-biological or microbiological processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public policy exclusions include medical/therapeutic methods, fundamental scientific/mathematical methods, living organisms (with microorganism exception), and essential biological processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entitlement to patent (Article 10–13)
rubrics_metrics.description: Party entitled to Patent is the Inventor or person who gets his/her assigns; jointly produced inventions are jointly owned; inventor presumed to be person first declared as inventor; employer may be Patent Holder for inventions produced in work relation unless agreed otherwise; inventor entitled to remuneration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines ownership presumptions, joint ownership, employer-employee rules, and inventor moral right to be named on certificate; remuneration rules and dispute resolution (Commercial Court) for disagreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remuneration for employee inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventor produced in work relation is entitled to Remuneration in accordance with agreement, taking into account economic benefit; may be lump sum, percentage, combination, or other agreed forms; disputes to Commercial Court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies bases of remuneration and remedies for unresolved calculation disputes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior user rights (Articles 14–18)
rubrics_metrics.description: A party who exploits an Invention at the same time the Invention is filed for a patent is still entitled to exploit the Invention even though a similar Invention is later granted a Patent; must file for recognition as prior user after grant and pay fee; cannot transfer prior user right except by inheritance; right expires with patent expiry; prior user cannot prohibit others from exploiting the Invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior user protection is limited (registration required after grant) and non-transferable (except inheritance); minister may revoke recognition for violation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of exclusive rights (Article 19)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Patent Holder has exclusive rights to exploit his/her Patent and prohibit others without approval from: making, using, selling, importing, renting out, delivering, or supplying for sale/rental/delivery of the patented product (product patent); or using the patented production process to make products (process patent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For process patents, prohibition on use of process applies only to imported products solely produced from use of patented process; exceptions exist for research/experimental/non-commercial analytical use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research/experimental exception
rubrics_metrics.description: In the event of educational, research, experimental, or analytical purposes, the prohibition may be exempted as long as it does not prejudice the proper interests of the patent holder and is non-commercial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits limited non-commercial research use; must not prejudice patent holder's interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Working requirement / local working (Article 20)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Patent holder is required to make the products or to use the process in Indonesia; doing so must encourage technology transfer, investment absorption and/or job vacancy provision; every Patent Holder or Licensee is required to pay annual fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Imposes obligation to exploit patented invention locally to promote national benefits; non-exploitation may trigger compulsory licensing or other measures (see later provisions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent term (Article 22 & 23)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Patent is granted for a period of 20 years as from the Filing Date; a Simple Patent is granted for 10 years as from the Filing Date; durations cannot be extended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Terms are fixed and non-extendable; dates recorded and published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application basis and language (Article 24)
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent is granted on the basis of an Application filed by Applicant or Proxy to the Minister in writing in Indonesian language and with payment of fee; application may be filed electronically or non-electronically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Language requirement is Indonesian; foreign-language descriptions must be translated within time limits or application is withdrawn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable scope per application (Article 24(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Every Application is filed for one Invention or a group of Inventions which are linked to each other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unity of invention requirement; if not linked, divisional applications required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required application contents (Article 25(1)–(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Application must at least contain: date, applicant/inventor/proxy names and addresses, country and first filing date if priority claimed; attached: title, description, claims, abstract, drawings if needed, power of attorney if filed by proxy, statement of ownership, transfer letter if applicant not inventor, microorganism deposit evidence if applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comprehensive list of formal and substantive attachments; missing items trigger notifications to correct per administrative examination rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficiency of disclosure / enablement (Article 25(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: The description of an Invention must clearly and completely describe how an Invention may be implemented by a person skilled in the art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Core enablement requirement: supports implementation by skilled person; tied to claims support (Article 25(4)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims support and clarity (Article 25(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim(s) of Invention must disclose clearly and consistently the field of technical Invention and be supported by the description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims must be supported by the written description; clarity and consistency required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genetic resources and traditional knowledge disclosure (Article 26)
rubrics_metrics.description: If related to genetic resources and/or traditional knowledge, the origin must be clearly and correctly mentioned in the description; benefit sharing/access to utilization exercised in accordance with legislation and treaties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obligation to disclose origin and comply with access/benefit-sharing legal framework; authoritative institution determines info.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proxy requirement for foreign applicants (Articles 27–28)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an Application is filed by a Proxy, the Proxy address is the domicile of the Applicant; applicants not residing/having permanent domicile in Indonesia must file by a Proxy in Indonesia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foreign applicants must engage an Indonesian-domiciled proxy (intellectual property consultant).

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority right timelines and documents (Article 30)
rubrics_metrics.description: An Application with Priority Rights must be filed within 12 months from the priority date; must be supplemented with validated priority document; validated priority document must be submitted to the Minister not later than 16 months from the priority date; otherwise application deemed filed without priority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict Paris Convention time limits; failure to timely supply validated documents forfeits priority claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative examination and filing date (Article 34)
rubrics_metrics.description: An Application which has fulfilled minimum requirements is given a Filing Date and recorded; minimum requirements include Application data, certain attachments, and receipt of payment of Application fee; if description is in foreign language, translation into Indonesian must be submitted within 30 days from Filing Date or application deemed withdrawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing date contingent on minimum formal requirements; translations have a tight 30-day cure period to avoid withdrawal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to cure formal deficiencies (Article 35–36)
rubrics_metrics.description: If requirements not completed, Minister notifies Applicant to complete within 3 months; extension options (2 months, then further 1 month with fee); emergency extensions possible up to 6 months after expiry with evidence; failure to complete results in application deemed withdrawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple staged extensions with fee and ability to request emergency extension; strict consequences for non-compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: First-to-file and competing applications (Article 37)
rubrics_metrics.description: If one similar Invention is filed in more than one Application by different Applicants on different dates, the Application with earlier Filing Date is considered to be granted Patent; if same Filing Date, Minister instructs Applicants to compromise and decide which application to grant within 6 months, otherwise Minister rejects the applications filed by several Applicants having the same Filing Date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: First-to-file rule with mechanism for same-day filings requiring applicant compromise; ministerial rejection if no compromise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments to application / scope narrowing (Articles 38–40)
rubrics_metrics.description: Application may be amended or divided before grant; amendments to description/claims may be carried out provided the amendment does not extend the scope of Invention of the original Application; adding more than 10 claims incurs fees for excess claims; application may be changed between Patent and Simple Patent without losing original filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments allowed but cannot introduce new matter / broaden scope; fees apply for excess claims; conversion between types keeps original date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisional application rules (Article 41)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an Application contains a group of Inventions not linked, Applicant may file divisional Application(s); divisional(s) must not extend beyond scope of protection requested in original application and are deemed filed on same date as original Filing Date; divisional requests must be timely or substantive examination will be limited to unity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Divisional retains priority/filing date but cannot broaden scope; timing is important to preserve rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of application (Article 43)
rubrics_metrics.description: Application may only be withdrawn by Applicant before the Minister decides to grant or refuse the Application; withdrawal filed in writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limited window for voluntary withdrawal (before final decision).

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of application documents (Article 45)
rubrics_metrics.description: All Application documents from the Filing Date to the announcement date are confidential, except for Inventor who does not act as the Applicant; any Person is required to preserve confidentiality; inventor-not-applicant may request copies with sufficient evidence and fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict confidentiality between filing and announcement, with limited access rights; minister responsible for confidentiality enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Announcement timing and content (Articles 46–48)
rubrics_metrics.description: Minister announces Applications that have fulfilled requirements not later than 7 Days after the period of 18 months from filing or priority date; earliest announcement may be 6 months at applicant request with fee; announcement lasts 6 months and must be visible and accessible, containing inventor/applicant names, title, filing/priority dates, abstract, classification, drawings if any, announcement number, application number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard 18-month publication rule with optional early publication for fee; announcement content specified for public inspection and opposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition / third-party observations during announcement (Article 49)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any Person may file opinion and/or opposition in writing during the announcement period; minister must communicate received opinions/oppositions to the Applicant within 7 days; Applicant may respond in writing within 30 days; minister uses these as additional information during substantive examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implements public participation: third-party observations/oppositions are considered by examiners as supplementary evidence but opposition is not an automatic blocking mechanism—applicant gets chance to respond.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-announcement for defense/security (Article 50)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an Invention concerns defense and security interests, the Minister may decide not to announce the Invention after consultation with relevant defense/security institutions; applicant is notified in writing and consulted documents are exempted from public disclosure; relevant institutions must preserve confidentiality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: National security carve-out allows withholding publication and imposes confidentiality obligations on consulted institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request and timing for substantive examination (Article 51)
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for substantive examination must be submitted in writing and is subject to fee; request filed not later than 36 months from Filing Date; failure to file or pay fee results in withdrawal; if requested early, substantive examination conducted after announcement expiry; divisional/substantive requests must be filed together where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 36-month window to request substantive examination (deferred prosecution allowed); missing the window results in abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive examination authority and standards (Articles 53–55)
rubrics_metrics.description: Substantive examinations are conducted by Examiners; Minister may use experts and facilities; examination is conducted in accordance with Articles on patentability (Art.3,4,5,7,8,9) and requirements (Art.25(3–4), 26, 39(2), 40, 41); Minister may request certified foreign prosecution/examination documents and use them as grounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner-led substantive review following the statute's substantive criteria; foreign examination results or decisions may be requested and used, but applicant can supplement explanations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision timelines for grant or refusal (Article 57)
rubrics_metrics.description: Minister decides to grant or refuse an Application not later than 30 months as from either the date of receipt of the request for substantive examination (if filed after announcement expiry) or the expiry of announcement period (if requested before expiry).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 30-month decision commitment measured from relevant procedural milestone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant procedures and certificate (Article 58)
rubrics_metrics.description: Minister grants if substantive examination shows compliance with provisions; Minister notifies Applicant in writing; within 2 months from notification, Minister issues a Patent certificate; Applicant may not withdraw or modify description/claims during that 2-month period; granted patent is recorded and published except for defense/security cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Issuance of patent certificate follows formal grant notice; prevents last-minute withdrawals or broadening post-grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of foreign examination/grant/refusal information (Article 55)
rubrics_metrics.description: Minister may request certified copies of foreign substantive examination results, granted patents, decisions of refusal, or invalidation to use as grounds for granting or refusing an Application with Priority Right; applicant may supplement with explanations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enables reliance on foreign office work-product for efficient examination, particularly for priority applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government use and compulsory licensing (concepts and definitions)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Law provides for Government use of patents and compulsory licensing in cases like defense/security, extreme urgency, or public interest; terms like 'reasonable Remuneration' are defined as balance between economic benefit to Patent Holder and State capability to pay; 'final' and 'binding' decisions and the roles of relevant ministers/institutions are specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Government use/compulsory license is subject to procedural protections, remuneration, and definitions; examples include pharmaceutical needs in public health emergencies, pesticides to prevent crop failure, or natural disaster responses (Article 109 examples).

rubrics_metrics.name: Remuneration and Royalty definitions (Articles 92, 115)
rubrics_metrics.description: Remuneration may be money or other agreed forms; 'Royalty' means remuneration awarded for utilization of right on Patent; 'reasonable Remuneration' means balance between economic benefit possibly obtained by Patent Holder and capability of State finance to pay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monetary and non-monetary compensation frameworks for forced or government use; intention to balance patent holder rights and public finances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effects of patent invalidation (Article 137–139)
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclusive rights of Patent Holder are removed since the Commercial Court decision has legal binding to invalidate a Patent; if patent invalidated, Licensee need not pay royalty to invalidated Patent Holder; partial invalidation requires claim adjustment by Patent Holder with Minister.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court invalidation has retroactive/ongoing effects on exclusivity and licensing payments; Minister must be informed of binding court decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confiscation, criminal enforcement and investigators' powers (Articles ~159–165)
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain civil servant investigators and authorities have powers to confiscate materials used to manufacture infringing goods, arrest, detain, set wanted lists, restrict entry/exit, and request assistance from police/Interpol/immigration; confiscated materials used as evidence cannot be reused to produce infringing goods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criminal enforcement includes strong investigatory and seizure powers, subject to legal process; special treatment to preserve evidence and confidentiality in process patents (reversed vindication).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reversed vindication for process patents (Article 145)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reversed vindication is applied considering the difficulty in handling disputes in patented process; judge may order Patent Holder to submit affidavit/copy of Patent certificate and preliminary evidence; judge may protect defendant's process confidentiality and close the court on request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects trade secrets/confidential process information in litigation while balancing evidentiary needs of patent holder; courts may proceed in closed sessions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation and public patent information system (Article 125)
rubrics_metrics.description: Documentation means compilation of archives/history of Patent from Application to final decisions in electronic and/or non-electronic documents; establishment of a national documentation and patent information network is to provide extensive information to the public to utilize technology development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates creation/maintenance of public patent documentation system for transparency and technology diffusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual fee payment rules and timing (Article 126–127)
rubrics_metrics.description: Annual fees are due with calculation examples provided; first payment timing depends on filing and grant dates with examples; second payment due not later than one month before same date as the Filing Date within protection period; resident patent holders may pay via Patent Holder or Proxy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies detailed timing and calculation methodology for annual maintenance fees; payment obligations and options for domiciled holders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural references to Ministerial Regulations and further provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Many procedural details (further provisions on terms, procedures, appointment/dismissal of experts, divisional application procedures, additional administrative rules) are delegated to Ministerial Regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statute sets substantive framework but delegates many administrative specifics to ministerial rules; practitioners must consult implementing regulations for operational details.
